title: Attention, Zoo Visitors
text:
Ding, dong! Attention, all zoo visitors. This is an important announcement.

The lion show starts in {number} minutes. Today Leo the Lion will jump through a hoop and {verb} on a big {adjective} ball. Please clap {adverb} so he knows you are watching.

We have found a lost item near the penguin pool. It is a small {noun} with {plural noun} on it. If it is yours, please come to the front gate.

The gorillas are having their nap. Please do not {verb} near their window. The last time someone did, the baby gorilla {past tense verb} for an hour.

The flamingos are {verb ending in ing} on one leg today. Please do not ask them to stop. They are very {adjective} about it.

Today's special at the snack stand is a {food} sandwich with a side of {plural noun}. Thank you, and have a {adjective} day!

title: My Zoo Field Trip Report
text:
Last Friday, my class went to the zoo. Our teacher, Mr. Ruiz, made us hold hands and walk {adverb}.

First we saw the giraffes. They are very tall and have long {plural noun}. One giraffe tried to nibble my friend Leo's {noun}, but Mr. Ruiz said it was just being friendly.

Next we visited the reptile house. A turtle was {verb ending in ing} in a tiny pool. I learned that turtles can live to be {number} years old and like to eat {plural noun}.

My favorite animal was the zebra. Its stripes are black and white and a little bit {color}. It {past tense verb} at me, so I waved back.

We ate lunch by the duck pond. A {adjective} duck took my {food} and ran away.

In conclusion, the zoo is {adjective}, and I would like to {verb} there every day. Next time I will bring a {noun}.

title: Penguin House Rules
text:
Welcome to the Penguin House! It is very cold in here, so please zip up your coat.

Rule one: Do not tap on the glass. The penguins do not like it, and they will {verb} at you.
Rule two: Lunch is at noon. Today the penguins will get ice cubes and {number} {plural noun}.
Rule three: Please walk {adverb}. The floor is very slippery, and so are the penguins.
Rule four: Our oldest penguin, Mr. Waddles, wears a tiny {adjective} bow tie. Please tell him he looks {adjective}.
Rule five: If a penguin starts {verb ending in ing}, it means she wants to play. You may wave your {body part} at her.
Rule six: No {plural noun} are allowed in here. Last week a boy brought some, and the penguins {past tense verb} for three days.
Rule seven: Please do not feed the penguins {food} or {plural noun}.

Thank you, and please waddle {adverb} on your way out!

title: Wanted: Zookeeper Helper
text:
The Sunnyside Zoo is looking for a helper! Do you love animals? Are you {adjective} and good at sharing? Then this job is for you.

Every morning, you will help brush the elephants' {plural noun}. Then you will sing to the koalas so they can {verb}. On Tuesdays, you will read a book about {plural noun} to the owls.

You will also help clean the hippo pool. Please wear a raincoat and a {noun} on your head. The hippos splash {adverb} when someone new is {verb ending in ing}.

The giraffes like their necks scratched with a {adjective} {noun}. Please do not let them {verb} near your lunch.

You will be paid with a big smile and {number} free {plural noun} every Friday. Our last helper {past tense verb} so much that the monkeys gave her a medal. To apply, draw a picture of a {animal} wearing a {noun}.

title: Your Guide to the Zoo Map
text:
Welcome to Pine Hill Zoo! Here is a quick guide to help you find your way.

Start at the front gate and walk past the big fountain. The fountain was a gift from a very {adjective} hippo named Gloria. If you toss a {noun} in, Gloria will {verb} for you.

Turn left at the Monkey House. You will hear the monkeys {verb ending in ing} before you see them. They are practicing a play about {plural noun}.

Keep walking until you reach the giant tortoise. He moves {adverb}, so he may still be where he was this morning. His name is {name}. Please wave your {body part} at him.

Next you will find the Bird Garden. The parrots there can say {number} words, but they only like to say "{silly word}."

The snack stand sells popcorn, juice, and {plural noun}. Our map ends at the gift shop, where you can buy a zoo hat or a {adjective} {noun}. Have a {adjective} visit!

title: Zoo News: The Elephant Learns to Paint
text:
Good morning! This is Zoo News, and we have a {adjective} story for you today.

Penny the Elephant has become an artist. Every morning, she holds a paintbrush with her trunk and paints pictures of {plural noun}. Her favorite color is {color}.

"We first noticed when she {past tense verb} on the wall of her barn," said zookeeper Mr. Tran. "So we gave her real paper. Now she paints {adverb} for hours and only stops for {food}."

Penny's paintings hang in the Zoo Cafe, right next to the {noun} machine. Her most famous one shows a giraffe holding a {noun}. People line up to {verb} in front of it.

Next week, Penny will teach an art class for the monkeys. So far the monkeys are mostly {verb ending in ing} and eating the {plural noun}. Penny says they are doing a {adjective} job.

That is all for Zoo News. Stay {adjective}, zoo fans!

title: A Day in the Life of a Zookeeper
text:
6:00 in the morning: My alarm went off. I put on my zoo shirt and my lucky {adjective} boots.
7:00: Breakfast for the animals! The giraffes got leaves, the bears got berries, and the parrots got {plural noun}.

9:00: The baby elephant would not get out of the pool. I asked her nicely to {verb}, but she {past tense verb} and splashed me instead.
12:00: Lunch! I ate with the penguins. One of them always tries to take my {noun}.

3:00: The kangaroos had a hopping contest. The winner hopped {number} times and won a {adjective} ribbon.
4:00: I gave the hippo a bath with soap and a {noun}. She said thank you {adverb}.
5:00: The lions were {verb ending in ing}, the monkeys were telling jokes, and the sloth was still eating breakfast.

8:00 at night: I fell asleep {adverb} and dreamed about {plural noun}.

title: Lunch for the Hungry Hippo
text:
Hector the Hippo is always hungry. Here is how the zookeepers make his favorite lunch.

You will need one giant watermelon, a wheelbarrow of lettuce, and {number} {plural noun}. You will also need a very {adjective} spoon.

First, cut the watermelon into slices as big as a {noun}. Next, mix the lettuce with a scoop of {food}. Stir it {adverb} until it looks like a salad. Then add a handful of {plural noun} and one {adjective} pickle.

Now for the best part. Carry the lunch to the pool and call, "Hector, it is time to {verb}!" He will swim over {verb ending in ing} with joy.

Last Tuesday, when Hector finished his lunch, he {past tense verb} and fell asleep in the sun. Next week the zookeepers will try adding a {noun}. Hippos are very {adjective} eaters.

title: Meet the Zoo's Oldest Tortoise
text:
This week, the Zoo Kids Club talked with Grandpa Shell, the oldest tortoise at our zoo. He is {number} years old.

Kids Club: What was the zoo like when you were young?
Grandpa Shell: Very {adjective}. The monkeys wore hats, and the giraffes played {plural noun} every afternoon.

Kids Club: What is your secret to staying happy?
Grandpa Shell: Eat your greens, take naps, and never {verb} after dinner. I also keep a {noun} under my shell for luck.

Kids Club: Who is your best friend?
Grandpa Shell: A {adjective} flamingo named Rosie. Every morning we go {verb ending in ing} together. She is much faster than me, but she waits {adverb}.

Kids Club: What do you do on your birthday?
Grandpa Shell: The zookeepers bring me a cake made of {plural noun} and {food}. Last year I {past tense verb} so hard that my shell wiggled.

Kids Club: Thank you, Grandpa Shell!
Grandpa Shell: You are welcome. Now please let me get back to {verb ending in ing} with my {noun}.

title: A Thank-You Note from the Panda
text:
Dear Visitors,

My name is Bao, and I am the panda who lives next to the gift shop. Thank you for visiting me this summer.

Thank you to the girl who waved at me with her {body part}. It made me feel very {adjective}. Thank you to the boy who sang me a song about {plural noun}. I liked it so much that I {past tense verb} all afternoon.

I know some of you wanted to see me {verb ending in ing}, but I was usually asleep. Next time, I will try to {verb} for you.

My favorite snack is still bamboo, but this summer I also tried a {noun}. It was {adjective}. The zookeeper says I chew {adverb}.

Please come back soon and bring {number} {plural noun}.

Your friend,
Bao
P.S. I will be sitting on my {adjective} rock, dreaming about {food}.
